name: kerryback

plugins.name: litdb
plugins.description: Personal literature + notes knowledge base: hybrid keyword+semantic search over your papers and notes, Zotero/Better BibTeX import, loose-PDF folder ingestion with full text, OpenAlex/Semantic Scholar discovery, and a citation graph. Local-first; the runtime installs into ~/.litdb on first use.

plugins.name: participation
plugins.description: Score class participation from a photo roster. Import Banner's Course Roster PDF to get every student's name and headshot, then tap 1-3 for amount and quality with optional notes while the class is fresh. Writes a row per student per meeting to participation.csv in the course's own folder. Local-first; the runtime installs into ~/.participation on first use.

plugins.name: voiceover
plugins.description: Turn a slide deck into a narrated MP4 video plus a transcript. Give it the PDF of your slides; Claude Code writes the narration, you edit it in a local app, and ElevenLabs voices it. Requires an ElevenLabs API key.

plugins.name: smithers
plugins.description: A personal email and calendar desk. Claude Code reads your Gmail and Calendar through a local connector, writes a fresh overview of what’s ahead for the next seven days every time you open the app, and parks drafted replies in a Compose tab you review and send yourself. Claude never sends mail and never deletes events — those stay your actions in the app. Local-first; state and Google tokens live in ~/.smithers.

plugins.name: screenshare
plugins.description: Let students put their own screen on the classroom projector. Claude runs a small WebRTC relay on the classroom computer and publishes it over a Cloudflare Quick Tunnel, so students join from an https link on their own laptops, pick a screen, window or tab, and wait in a queue while the instructor chooses who is shown. Video goes browser to browser — direct when the campus network allows it, through a TURN relay when segmentation blocks the direct path. Nothing is recorded and nothing is written to disk. Runs on Windows, macOS or Linux; on a locked-down classroom machine it can fetch its own cloudflared without admin rights.

plugins.name: poll
plugins.description: Put a question to the class and show the answers on the projector. Type `/poll What's the capital of France? Paris, Topeka or Frankfurt` and it goes up immediately — Claude reads the sentence, works out that it is multiple choice and which option is right, and the app runs it: multiple choice, word clouds, confidence scales, numeric estimates and rankings, each drawn live as answers arrive. `/poll <file>` runs a poll written before class instead, and both land in one session and one results file. Students answer from their own devices over a Cloudflare Quick Tunnel. Anonymous by design: no names, no roster, nothing stored per student, and concept-check results stay hidden while voting is open so the room doesn't follow the leading bar. Needs cloudflared.

plugins.name: survey
plugins.description: Put a question to the class and show the answers on the projector. Type `/survey What's the capital of France? Paris, Topeka or Frankfurt` and it goes up immediately — Claude reads the sentence, works out that it is multiple choice and which option is right, and the app runs it: multiple choice, select all that apply, word clouds, confidence scales, numeric estimates and rankings, each drawn live as answers arrive. `/survey <file>` loads a poll written before class, and the projector's menu jumps to any question at any time, so a prepared class is a set of questions to reach for rather than a queue to walk. Students answer at a fixed public address, so there is no tunnel to start and nothing to install beyond an API token. Anonymous by design: no names, no roster, nothing stored per student, and concept-check results stay hidden while voting is open so the room doesn't follow the leading bar.

plugins.name: shoji
plugins.description: Build a Quarto reveal.js slide deck in the Shoji style — a plum, pale-gray and dusty-blue theme derived from the PowerPoint design of the same name, with an offset panel frame, letter-spaced titles, cards, callouts, stats, steps, and half-bleed picture layouts, rendered to HTML and exported to PDF. Use when the user invokes /shoji, asks for a shoji deck by name, or is editing a deck already built with this theme. For a general "make me slides" with no style named, prefer the pptx skill.

plugins.name: finance-data
plugins.description: Fetch free financial, market, and economic data (prices, fundamentals, SEC filings, macro series, asset-pricing factors) from Yahoo, Stooq, SEC EDGAR, FRED, Ken French, FinnHub, FMP, and US Treasury, and save it as CSV.

plugins.name: wrds
plugins.description: Empirical asset-pricing data from WRDS (CRSP v2/Compustat) and Open Source Asset Pricing: extractable Python building blocks for connect (without a 2FA prompt), pull, merge, market cap aggregated across share classes, the CRSP-Compustat link, book equity, accounting alignment and firm age — every query run against live WRDS. Surfaces the constructions that are genuine decisions rather than common practice (Ken French vs Drechsler's WRDS script vs OpenAP, and the 4- vs 6-month reporting lag) instead of picking silently, and ships twelve WRDS reference scripts.

plugins.name: critique
plugins.description: Critique work Claude produced and say what to do about it. Parallel reviewer agents -- correctness traced back to the files that produced each number, clarity, a devil's advocate that reads the code rather than the prose, and a referee lane for academic papers that hands off to econ-review when it is installed. Every finding must carry located evidence, a consequence specific to this work, a proportionate repair, and a condition that would defeat it; Claude then argues against its own reviewers before showing you anything. Delivers an HTML guide that leads with the verdict and lays out the alternative paths forward -- narrow the claim, run one decisive check, reframe, redesign, or ship -- as choices with costs, not as a checklist. Heavyweight: it fans out multiple subagents.

plugins.name: human-write
plugins.description: Write and edit academic prose that reads as human, not machine-generated: varied sentence rhythm, no formulaic AI tells (delve, however-at-every-turn, the not-X-but-Y contrast, three-item everything), and structure driven by the argument rather than a template. Defaults to scholarly register (journal articles, working papers, referee reports, grant proposals). Works when drafting fresh and when revising a draft.

plugins.name: elegant-pdf
plugins.description: Create elegant, branded documents from a small HTML design system rendered to PDF or image with headless Chrome — one-page flyers/announcements (2x JPEG or clickable PDF) and multi-page programs, reports, and handbooks (clickable PDF with cover, running footer, and page numbers). Default palette is Rice Business navy + gold; recolor by editing one block.

plugins.name: research
plugins.description: Set up a research repository several people and their Claudes can share without tripping over each other: per-author folders, portable paths derived rather than configured, one canonical dataset with recorded promotion, provenance read out of the code, a git-enforced round lock, and a generated CLAUDE.md that makes the whole thing self-explaining. Optional two-build (analyst/replicator) protocol for empirical work, an OpenRouter debate panel, and an Overleaf mirror of the paper directory via the git bridge for teams where only some coauthors use Overleaf. Works on a new project or an existing one that grew organically. Ships a vendored writing guide -- economics section formulas and style rules merged with the prose standards that keep drafts from reading as machine-written -- binding for everything in draft/, and it learns: hooks capture the prose corrections you give, /style-learn turns them into rules you accept one at a time and writes them into the guide itself, and the rules your project added are extracted into context at the start of every session. One standard, never a second file of conventions to disagree with it.

description: Authoring and teaching skills for Claude Code: narrated video from slide decks, Quarto slide decks, free financial/economic data, and adversarial work review.
